title: session_bus.v1
description: Session-bus message and queue-row schemas (M1). Validated by scripts/coordination/session_bus.py. Owning handoff: handoffs/active/session-bus-thin-dispatcher.md. Single-writer ownership is a protocol property enforced by the CLI's `validate` lint, NOT by this schema, so writer violations report distinctly from structural failures.

id.description: msg-<compact-utc>-<seq>-<writer>, e.g. msg-20260727T182214Z-1-claude-main. Lexicographically sortable; deliberately free of offset punctuation so the id is a single clean token.

kind.description: R11 (2026-08-13): the compute-window dialogue. A main that needs a compute window writes `compute-request` (payload: task, requested window, device/region, est_h, release-condition) routed to `inference`; `inference` answers `compute-grant` (accepted window + boundaries) or `compute-deny` (reason + what to do next). Before these kinds existed the dialogue ran as `kind=status` + `payload.request_kind=compute-request|compute-grant|compute-deny`, which satisfied intent but violated the letter of BUS_PROTOCOL rule 11.

corr_ids.description: C23 (2026-08-11): every routed message this ONE row dispositions, in addition to any scalar `corr_id`. Added because the previous rule was not performable: clearing triage took one corr_id per item, so a session holding a single answer for N routed items had no compliant way to send it once, and BUS_PROTOCOL.md told authors to 'write it once and reference it' while no mechanism to reference it existed. Measured 2026-07-29: 9 byte-identical payloads in 10 minutes from one careful main, hours after that discipline rule was codified — and fan-out makes it N dispositions x M routing targets. Purely additive: the scalar still works and is still right for a genuinely per-item answer. Use this ONLY when one answer really does cover every id listed; N distinct answers still want N rows, because a reader who cannot tell N answers from one answer repeated N times has lost the signal the queue exists to carry.

operator_signature_needed.description: C49 (2026-08-12): author-set POSITIVE marker — true means this message needs A HUMAN'S signature, not a named agent's action. Deliberately declared here at the generic `payload` level, not inside a per-kind `allOf` branch, because it is legal on ANY kind, not one. Replaces an INFERRED predicate (`kind in {token-request, defect}` OR `severity`/`priority == CRITICAL`) measured 2026-08-12 against 267 live inbox rows: 116 carried `action_required` (agent-action, never operator), only 8 satisfied the old predicate, and just 7 overlapped — near-disjoint in both directions. Every one of those 8 was `kind: defect` (fleet-internal engineering work); not one was a `token-request`, the only kind that IS an operator gate by definition. `_is_operator_item` (scripts/coordination/session_bus_coordinator.py) is now `payload.operator_signature_needed is True` OR `kind == 'token-request'` — token-request stays because a token IS the operator's signature, and dropping it would silence that channel. Absent or false is the default: `action_required`/`needs_routing_to` route to a named agent, never the operator, and CRITICAL severity does not imply operator-ness either.

relayed_src.description: Set by the coordinator-daemon when it relays an agent-authored outbox message into a recipient inbox: the source msg id. Carries the dedupe key so relay is idempotent across ticks (defect C2, 2026-07-28). Absent on daemon-generated messages.

_renamed_from.description: Migration provenance: the roster id this row was authored under, before the 2026-07-29 rename (claude-gpu-lane / claude-main / fable-auditor / codex -> the current ids). Written by the rename migration onto the 217 rows it rewrote, so `from`/`to` could be updated without losing who actually sent the message. PERMITTED 2026-08-11 (C34, second half): the migration wrote it, `additionalProperties: false` forbade it, and the relay therefore refused all 217 rows — including five operator token-requests stranded for two weeks. Stripping it was the alternative and is not available: an outbox has exactly one writer and it is not the daemon, so the choice was to accept the provenance or lose the mail. Historical only; nothing should write this field again.
_renamed_from.$comment: Underscore-prefixed by convention: tool-written provenance, not agent-authored content.

assignee.description: ADDRESSING (2026-08-12, Phase 4): the ONE roster id that must ACT on this message. `action_required: true` REQUIRES an addressee that resolves to exactly one party — `assignee` is that field, and `append` refuses `action_required` with more than one routing target. (Transitional: a legacy row with `needs_routing_to` of length 1 and no `assignee` still resolves, so history keeps working; new rows should set `assignee`.) Measured 2026-08-12: 499 `action_required` rows sat across the fleet's inboxes and only 86 were sole-target, so 83% of what an agent had to triage was not its own — because one boolean applied to every member of `needs_routing_to` and the schema had no way to say 'read this, you owe nothing'. That way is `cc`. N agents each owing a DISTINCT action is N messages, not one message with N targets.

cc.description: ADDRESSING (2026-08-12, Phase 4): REACH-ONLY readers. A cc entry never implies an action, never owes an ack or a disposition, and is cleared by advancing a cursor — it appears in `drain --triage` as a one-line FYI, never as a MUST-ACT item. Entries must be roster ids (`append` refuses unknowns). Use this for the fleet-wide report; use `assignee` for the one party that must do something.

cc_delivery.description: Tool-written marker set by the coordinator-daemon relay on a CC copy: this delivery reached you because you were on `cc`/`needs_routing_to`, NOT because you are the addressee. The copy PRESERVES the original `to` for exactly this reason — before 2026-08-12 the relay rewrote `to` to each fan-out target, so 100% of delivered rows looked directly addressed and a CC was structurally indistinguishable from an assignment.

needs_routing_to.description: STRUCTURAL routing intent (2026-07-29): the roster ids this message must REACH, beyond the transport `to`. Added because two routed messages were missed when routing intent lived as prose inside `payload` and a context-economy truncation cut exactly the sentence carrying it. Prose is not a routing channel: tools act on this field. Entries must be roster ids (append refuses unknowns). A message with this field appears in each named agent's `triage` standing queue until that agent dispositions it by corr_id from its own outbox — advancing a cursor never clears it.

action_required.description: STRUCTURAL action intent (2026-07-29). SINCE 2026-08-12 IT IS SINGULAR: exactly ONE party may owe the action, named by `assignee` (or, transitionally, a single-entry `needs_routing_to`, else a concrete `to`). `append` REFUSES `action_required: true` with more than one routing target — reach-only readers belong in `cc`. The routed-to agent must ACT, not merely receive. Stays in their `triage` queue until dispositioned by an outbox row with matching corr_id that is either a substantive kind (anything but a bare ack) or an ack with payload.disposition in {done, declined, handed-off, superseded}. A bare ack marks it acked-but-unactioned and it KEEPS appearing: acknowledgment is receipt, not action. `append` refuses action_required on to='*' with needs_routing_to unset — intent with no addressee is the failure shape this field exists to kill.

payload.description: AUD-2 (2026-08-12): a typed dispatch vocabulary. Measured across the 55 task-assign messages on the live bus: 171 DISTINCT payload keys — which is why no content rule about a dispatch was mechanizable, and why briefs asserted constraints nobody imposed. The fields below are that vocabulary. `task_text` is REQUIRED AT AUTHORING (enforced in `cmd_append`, not by `required` here, because the 119 pre-migration task-assign rows on the live bus must keep validating — authoring-side enforcement only). `additionalProperties` is deliberately NOT false for the same reason; `append` WARNS on keys outside this vocabulary instead of refusing.

task_text.description: REQUIRED at authoring. The dispatch IDENTITY: the backlog row's TEXT, verbatim. Not a line reference — anchor rot measured 34.5% queue-wide on 2026-08-11 (up from 27% twelve days earlier), so `file.md:LINE` names a different row every few weeks while the text keeps resolving.

row_ref.description: OPTIONAL HINT ONLY — `handoff.md:LINE` or `handoff.md#anchor`. Demoted from identity to hint on 2026-08-12: when it disagrees with `task_text`, the text wins. Re-resolve with scripts/coordination/backlog_row_check.py --row "<text>".

screened_by.description: RECEIPT that the row was screened before dispatch, e.g. "backlog_row_check.py@2026-08-12T09:14Z:WELL-FORMED". A screener proves WELL-FORMED, not STILL-NEEDED — four of eight rows screened on 2026-08-12 were already satisfied in reality — so this is evidence the check ran, never evidence the premise holds.

expected_occupancy.description: F-14 fix: how long this work should HOLD the hardware. The coordinator queued seconds-long work at a card that needed hours of occupancy; nothing in the dispatch made the mismatch expressible, so nobody could see it. Declaring it forces the question at composition time.

basis.description: where the estimate comes from (a prior run, a queue field, a guess said out loud)

constraints.description: F-20 fix: a brief asserted `lanes: [none]` that the roster never imposed. A RESTATED constraint cites the line it derives from, or it is not a constraint — it is the author's recollection wearing the roster's authority. THE TYPED FORM IS THE ARRAY: each entry an object with `constraint` + a REQUIRED `source`. The bare-string form is legacy only (a prose blob of constraints, source unstated, which is exactly the F-20 shape) — it still validates so the 119 pre-migration rows keep working, and `append` WARNS on it.

source.description: file:line, msg id, or config key the constraint derives from

brief_path.description: Path to the full brief. REQUIRED once the payload exceeds the size cap enforced in `cmd_append` (draft-7 has no size keyword, so the cap lives in code): a dispatch too big to read in a triage report belongs in a file the assignee opens, with the row carrying the pointer.

payload.description: Pre-validation is MANDATORY: an operator command that fails is a defect row attributed to the requesting agent.

R4 — request that a holder give its lease back. Authority is checked against config.yaml authority.lease_grant; an unauthorised sender is rejected with a defect row. Revocation is ALWAYS quiesce-and-drain at the holder's next boundary (fabric axiom 4) — never a kill.

yield_to.description: task_id or priority class this yields to

payload.description: How work ENTERS the queue. Agents never write queue.jsonl — they propose, and the coordinator-daemon transcribes (pure bookkeeping, no judgment). gating is mandatory here for the same reason it is mandatory on the row: without it a lease revocation has no defined fallback set.

spec_ref.description: owning handoff (+ checkbox anchor) — the spec stays OUT of the row

classification.description: how lane/gating were decided — 'heuristic' means provisional

task_text.description: AUD-2: the backlog row's TEXT. Transcribed onto the queue row so the daemon's own task-assign can carry the dispatch identity without re-reading the handoff.

payload.description: AUD-4 (2026-08-12): a finding may CORRECT an earlier message. Five corrections were silently missing from the 2026-08-12 wrap-up because a correction was indistinguishable from any other finding, so nothing could enumerate them. `corrects` makes the relation structural and `session_bus.py corrections --agent <id>` generates the wrap-up section from it; an omitted correction is now a visible omission rather than an invisible one. Both fields are OPTIONAL: an ordinary finding corrects nothing.

corrects.description: the msg id this finding corrects

provenance.description: how the corrected fact is known. `operator-verbatim` = the operator's own words, quotable; `paraphrase` = the operator's meaning in the author's words; `inferred` = the author's conclusion from evidence, which the operator never said.

payload.description: R11 (2026-08-13): a requesting main asks `inference` for a compute window. `window` names the requested boundaries (start/end or duration); `device_region` names the region/device; `est_h` the estimated duration; `release_condition` states what the requester will report/do to release the window. Should be authored with `needs_routing_to: ["inference"]` (enforced by `_check_routing_intent` for resolvability, not by schema).

task.description: task identity — the backlog row TEXT, same discipline as task-assign payload.task_text

window.description: requested window boundaries, e.g. "now for up to 1h" or explicit start/end ts

est_h.description: estimated duration of the window in hours

release_condition.description: what the requester will report or do when the window can be released

payload.description: R11 (2026-08-13): `inference` accepts a compute-request. `window` states the ACCEPTED boundaries (which may differ from the requested ones); `boundaries` carries any operating constraints on the window.

task.description: the task this grant covers — mirrors the compute-request's `task`

window.description: accepted window boundaries, e.g. "granted immediately for up to 1h"

device_region.description: confirmed region/device, if narrower or different from the request

boundaries.description: operating constraints on the window (what the requester must/must not do while holding it)

release_condition.description: what the requester must report or do to release the window (echo or refine the request's release_condition)

payload.description: R11 (2026-08-13): `inference` refuses a compute-request. `reason` explains the refusal; `next` tells the requester what to do instead (retry at a stated time, use a different region, run without compute, ...).

task.description: the task this denial covers — mirrors the compute-request's `task`

next.description: what to do next — e.g. "retry after <ts>", "use CPU region q0-q3 instead", "proceed without compute"

queue_row.title: session_bus.queue.v1
queue_row.description: Appended by the coordinator-daemon ONLY. Fold is latest-row-per-task_id-wins (batch_ledger.reconcile semantics). Agents propose and report; they never write this file.

gating.description: R4 prerequisite — REQUIRED. Without it a lease revocation has no defined fallback set and the keep-working rule cannot be honoured.

contention_class.description: R5 pausability. exclusive-contiguous = decision-gating timing run, never paused.

spec_ref.description: spec stays OUT of the row

task_text.description: AUD-2 (2026-08-12): the backlog row's TEXT — the dispatch identity, carried from the task-propose payload at intake so the daemon's own `task-assign` can populate payload.task_text without re-reading the handoff. `spec_ref` remains the pointer; this is the identity.

screened_by.description: AUD-2: receipt that backlog_row_check ran on this row before it entered the queue.

expected_occupancy.description: AUD-2 / F-14: how long the work should hold the hardware; copied verbatim onto the task-assign payload.

replay_eligible.description: R9 — result obtainable by deterministic replay over banked outputs: needs no lane, no claim, no token.

role_affinity.description: R3 — the stack role whose resource profile this task resembles, used to look the task up in the MEASURED contention matrix (per-role-pair verdicts). Distinct from contention_class, which is the pausability axis. Absent means co-residency is not applicable to this task, not that it is permitted.

revoking.description: R4 — the coordinator-agent has asked for this lease back. The task keeps its current status because it IS still running; the holder stops accepting new work and releases at its next boundary (axiom 4). A revoking task is never re-assigned while still held.
